_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-11 16:26:48Z)**_

Here's where new category name entry happens:

**Modal component (desktop)**
- [NewCategoryModal.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/NewCategoryModal.tsx) — the actual text input field, built on `SingleInputModal` with placeholder "Category name"

**Triggering it**
- [BudgetCategories.tsx:271](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BudgetCategories.tsx#L271) (desktop budget sidebar "add category" row/button)
- [mobile/budget/BudgetPage.tsx:188](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/budget/BudgetPage.tsx#L188) (mobile equivalent, dispatches `{ name: 'new-category' }` modal)
- [Modals.tsx:240](packages/desktop-client/src/components/Modals.tsx#L240) — modal registry that wires `'new-category'` to `NewCategoryModal`

**Type/state definitions**
- [modalsSlice.ts:450](packages/desktop-client/src/modals/modalsSlice.ts#L450) — defines the `new-category` modal's props (`onValidate`, `onSubmit`)

**Related (renaming an existing category, not creating)**
- [SidebarCategory.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/SidebarCategory.tsx) — inline editable name field for existing categories, and [SidebarGroup.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/SidebarGroup.tsx) for category groups (uses `NewCategoryGroupModal.tsx` for new groups, same pattern).

The actual submit logic (creating the category via the mutation) lives in [budget/mutations.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/budget/mutations.ts).

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-11 16:37:42Z)**_

Yes — it **blocks the save**, not just informs. The check runs inside `useSaveCategoryMutation`'s `mutationFn` and returns early (`return;`) before calling `createCategory.mutateAsync`/`updateCategory.mutateAsync`, so nothing is sent to the backend and the category is never created/renamed. The user just sees the error toast, same as the existing duplicate-name behavior.

One gap worth flagging: on **mobile**, creating a *brand-new* category goes through a different path — [BudgetPage.tsx:192](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/budget/BudgetPage.tsx#L192) calls `createCategory.mutate(...)` (`useCreateCategoryMutation`) directly, not `useSaveCategoryMutation`. So my check currently only applies to:
- Desktop create + rename (both go through `useSaveCategoryMutation` via `_onSaveCategory`)
- Mobile **rename** (`saveCategory.mutate` at [BudgetPage.tsx:260](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/budget/BudgetPage.tsx#L260))

Mobile **create** doesn't hit this check yet — a mobile user could still submit a >50 character name for a new category.

Want me to move the length check into `useCreateCategoryMutation` (and/or `onValidate` on the mobile modal) so it's enforced on that path too?

1	// Minimal connection mock used by desktop-client component tests.
2	//
3	// This mirrors `@actual-app/core`'s test-only mock implementation so that
4	// `useSpreadsheet()` and other code paths can call `send()` and receive a
5	// promise with a stable shape.
6	
7	type Listener = (args: unknown) => void;
8	type Handler = (args: unknown) => unknown | Promise<unknown>;
9	
10	let listeners = new Map<string, Array<Listener>>();
11	let serverHandler:
12	  | null
13	  | ((msg: { name: string; args: unknown; catchErrors: boolean }) => unknown) =
14	  null;
15	
16	export const initServer = (handlers: Record<string, Handler>) => {
17	  serverHandler = msg => {
18	    const { name, args, catchErrors } = msg;
19	    if (handlers[name]) {
20	      return Promise.resolve().then(() => {
21	        const promise = Promise.resolve(handlers[name](args));
22	
23	        if (catchErrors) {
24	          return promise.then(
25	            data => ({ data }),
26	            error => ({ error }),
27	          );
28	        }
29	
30	        return promise;
31	      });
32	    }
33	  };
34	};
35	
36	export const clearServer = async () => {
37	  serverHandler = null;
38	  listeners = new Map();
39	};
40	
41	export const serverPush = (name: string, args: unknown) => {
42	  void Promise.resolve().then(() => {
43	    const listens = listeners.get(name);
44	    if (listens) {
45	      listens.forEach(listener => {
46	        listener(args);
47	      });
48	    }
49	  });
50	};
51	
52	export const send = async (
53	  name: string,
54	  args: unknown,
55	  { catchErrors = false } = {},
56	) => {
57	  if (serverHandler) {
58	    return serverHandler({ name, args, catchErrors });
59	  } else {
60	    throw new Error('`send` called with no mock server installed');
61	  }
62	};
63	
64	export const sendCatch = (name: string, args: unknown) => {
65	  return send(name, args, { catchErrors: true });
66	};
67	
68	export const listen = (name: string, cb: Listener) => {
69	  if (!listeners.get(name)) {
70	    listeners.set(name, []);
71	  }
72	
73	  listeners.get(name)!.push(cb);
74	
75	  return () => {
76	    const arr = listeners.get(name) ?? [];
77	    listeners.set(
78	      name,
79	      arr.filter(cb_ => cb_ !== cb),
80	    );
81	  };
82	};
83

37	  };

45	type AddNotificationPayload = {

50	};

52	  inset: NotificationsState['inset'];
53	} | null;

55	const notificationsSlice = createSlice({

57	  initialState,

62	        id: action.payload.notification.id || uuidv4(),
63	      };
64	
65	      if (state.notifications.find(n => n.id === notification.id)) {
66	        return;
67	      }
68	      state.notifications = [...state.notifications, notification];
69	    },
70	    addGenericErrorNotification(state) {
71	      const notification: NotificationWithId = {

73	        type: 'error',
74	        message: t(
75	          'Something internally went wrong. You may want to restart the app if anything looks wrong. ' +
76	            'Please report this as a new issue on GitHub.',
77	        ),
78	      };
79	      state.notifications = [...state.notifications, notification];
80	    },
81	    removeNotification(
82	      state,
83	      action: PayloadAction<RemoveNotificationPayload>,
84	    ) {
85	      state.notifications = state.notifications.filter(
86	        notif => notif.id !== action.payload.id,
87	      );
88	    },
89	    setNotificationInset(
90	      state,
91	      action: PayloadAction<SetNotificationInsetPayload>,
92	    ) {
93	      state.inset = action.payload?.inset ? action.payload.inset : {};
94	    },
95	  },
96	  extraReducers: builder => {
97	    builder.addCase(resetApp, () => initialState);

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

import {
  clearServer,
  initServer,
} from '@actual-app/core/platform/client/connection';
import type { CategoryEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
import { renderHook, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import i18next from 'i18next';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

import { createTestAppStore, TestProviders } from '#mocks';
import type { AppStore } from '#redux/store';

import {
  CATEGORY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH,
  useCreateCategoryMutation,
  useSaveCategoryMutation,
} from './mutations';

vi.mock(
  '@actual-app/core/platform/client/connection',
  () => import('#mocks/connection'),
);

// With no translation resources loaded, i18next echoes the key back with
// interpolation applied - matching what the notification messages render.
void i18next.init({
  lng: 'en',
  interpolation: { escapeValue: false },
});

function wrapperFor(store: AppStore) {
  return function Wrapper({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
    return <TestProviders store={store}>{children}</TestProviders>;
  };
}

function getNotifications(store: AppStore) {
  return store.getState().notifications.notifications;
}

const tooLongName = 'a'.repeat(CATEGORY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH + 1);
const maxLengthName = 'a'.repeat(CATEGORY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH);

afterEach(async () => {
  await clearServer();
});

describe('useCreateCategoryMutation', () => {
  it('rejects a name over the character limit without contacting the server', async () => {
    const createCategoryHandler = vi.fn(async () => 'new-id');
    initServer({ 'category-create': createCategoryHandler });

    const store = createTestAppStore();
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useCreateCategoryMutation(), {
      wrapper: wrapperFor(store),
    });

    await result.current.mutateAsync({
      name: tooLongName,
      groupId: 'group1',
      isIncome: false,
      isHidden: false,
    });

    expect(createCategoryHandler).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(getNotifications(store)).toMatchObject([
      { type: 'error', message: expect.stringContaining('50') },
    ]);
  });

  it('allows a name at the character limit', async () => {
    const createCategoryHandler = vi.fn(async () => 'new-id');
    initServer({ 'category-create': createCategoryHandler });

    const store = createTestAppStore();
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useCreateCategoryMutation(), {
      wrapper: wrapperFor(store),
    });

    await result.current.mutateAsync({
      name: maxLengthName,
      groupId: 'group1',
      isIncome: false,
      isHidden: false,
    });

    expect(createCategoryHandler).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      name: maxLengthName,
      groupId: 'group1',
      isIncome: false,
      hidden: false,
    });
    expect(getNotifications(store)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('useSaveCategoryMutation', () => {
  function newCategory(name: string): CategoryEntity {
    return {
      id: 'new',
      name,
      group: 'group1',
      is_income: false,
      hidden: false,
    };
  }

  beforeEach(() => {
    initServer({
      'get-categories': async () => ({ grouped: [], list: [] }),
    });
  });

  it('rejects a name over the character limit without contacting the server', async () => {
    const createCategoryHandler = vi.fn(async () => 'new-id');
    initServer({
      'get-categories': async () => ({ grouped: [], list: [] }),
      'category-create': createCategoryHandler,
    });

    const store = createTestAppStore();
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useSaveCategoryMutation(), {
      wrapper: wrapperFor(store),
    });

    await result.current.mutateAsync({ category: newCategory(tooLongName) });

    expect(createCategoryHandler).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(getNotifications(store)).toMatchObject([
      { type: 'error', message: expect.stringContaining('50') },
    ]);
  });

  it('allows a name at the character limit', async () => {
    const createCategoryHandler = vi.fn(async () => 'new-id');
    initServer({
      'get-categories': async () => ({ grouped: [], list: [] }),
      'category-create': createCategoryHandler,
    });

    const store = createTestAppStore();
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useSaveCategoryMutation(), {
      wrapper: wrapperFor(store),
    });

    await result.current.mutateAsync({ category: newCategory(maxLengthName) });

    await waitFor(() => expect(createCategoryHandler).toHaveBeenCalled());
    expect(getNotifications(store)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-11 17:57:46Z)**_

Yes. `yarn start` → `start:browser` runs `vite --mode=browser`, which is Vite's dev server — it compiles TS/TSX on-the-fly per request (not a one-time bundle) and pushes updates over HMR websocket whenever you save a file. So edits to `mutations.ts` and `BudgetPage.tsx` are picked up automatically; you don't need a separate build step.

A couple of caveats specific to what we changed:

- **HMR for hooks isn't always granular.** Since `useCreateCategoryMutation`/`useSaveCategoryMutation` are hooks (not components), Vite's React Fast Refresh may not always hot-swap the new mutation logic cleanly. If your test doesn't reflect the change after saving, do a manual browser refresh (not a restart of `yarn start`) — that's enough to pick up the new module.
- **loot-core (`@actual-app/core`)** is a separate workspace, but Vite resolves it via the package.json `"development"` export condition straight to its TS source, so it's also compiled on-the-fly — no separate watch/build needed for that either.
- If you're also running `start:server-dev`, that starts the sync server and frontend together, but the frontend piece behaves the same way.

So: run `yarn start`, open `http://localhost:3001`, and just refresh the tab after saving if changes don't auto-apply.

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.

The `categories update <id>` command is at [categories.ts:66-89](packages/cli/src/commands/categories.ts#L66-L89).

To answer directly: no, it does not separately prompt the user to type the category name. `--name <name>` is a Commander option value supplied on the command line (e.g. `actual categories update abc123 --name "Groceries"`), not an interactive prompt — there's no `input.ts` prompt call in this action, it just reads `cmdOpts.name` straight from the parsed CLI args and, if present, puts it into `fields.name` before calling `api.updateCategory(id, fields)`.

That also means it currently has no length validation — unlike `create`, which I just added a 100-character check to.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-11 15:47:08Z)**_

Yes — despite the command being called "update," `--name` does set a brand-new string value into the same `name` field that `create` writes (`fields.name = cmdOpts.name` → `api.updateCategory(id, fields)`). There's nothing about it being an existing category that makes long names safer; the data ends up in the same column with the same constraints. So the same 100-char limit should logically apply here too — otherwise `create --name <101 chars>` would be rejected but `update --name <101 chars>` on that same category would silently succeed, which is an inconsistent (and confusing) rule.

Want me to add the same `validateCategoryNameLength` check to the `update` action?
